additional_info.subject: RE: 0369150 - ID0369150-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / RN 170002886] Left charging point does not go into charging CRM:00641000588
additional_info.body:
Dear Ramona,
I hope you are doing well.
Regarding the reported issue, we have reviewed the logs and observed that the session was aborted during the cable check. As per the standard, the cable check should complete within 60 seconds; otherwise, it will stop, which is consistent with our analysis.
Additionally, during our analysis, we checked the EVMAC of the vehicles we were trying to charge and found that they are from Volkswagen Group of America. Therefore, we suspect there might be an integration issue to this particular brand.
Kindly refer the below log analysis where we can see charging session has been aborted due to cable check timeout
2024-07-16T10:20:34.290914+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] 2024-07-16 10:20:34 - Error: "FEC_GENERAL_TIMEOUT_IN_CABLE_CHECK"
2024-07-16T10:39:26.348516+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] 2024-07-16 10:39:26 - Error: "FEC_GENERAL_TIMEOUT_IN_CABLE_CHECK"
2024-07-16T10:22:18.454964+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] 2024-07-16 10:22:18 - Error: "FEC_GENERAL_TIMEOUT_IN_CABLE_CHECK"
2024-07-16T10:18:48.000000+00:00 secc [daemon:notice] SECC[822]: {"type":"stop_charging","timestamp":1721125128491,"chargerId":"secc2300-09850","outlet":"2","outletType":"CCS","payload":{"source":"App","user":"internal"}}
We suggest performing some sessions with other brands to determine the cause of the failure.
Please let us know the update once you checked with other brand vehicles.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav Malokar

RE: AW: 0369150 - ID0369150-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / RN 170002886] Left charging point does not go into charging CRM:00641000588
additional_info.body:
Dear Ramona,
Hope you are doing well.
We have reviewed the logs on AWS CloudWatch and found some anomalies regarding the contactor Q21-22, which is used for charging via the DC1 outlet. During the cable check, the contactor's feedback goes into an abnormal state. According to the standard for cable checks, both side contactors should close properly for the cable check to be performed successfully.
Please refer to the attached log file for reference.
In this scenario, we recommend arranging some charging sessions on Monday or Tuesday so that we can monitor the situation via SSH. Meanwhile, we will coordinate with R&D to take the necessary access.
Please let us know the prior so that we can arrange for access,
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -

Mit freundlichen Grüßen

additional_info.body:
Dear Team,
Hope you are doing well,
Yesterday, we conducted a site intervention to troubleshoot the ongoing issues. During our discussion with the service technician, it was revealed that there had been a prior intervention where the outlets experienced water ingress, and the customer attempted to dry the outlets.
Following this, there was a second site visit from the regional team (Marius) to train the technicians at Breilmann KG. During this visit, the KF12/11 module was replaced to determine if it would resolve the outlet issues. Feedback from the customer indicated that there have been consistent problems with the outlet.
Given this context, it's unclear why there was no mention of the water ingress issue or the customer's attempt to dry the outlets in the ticket description when ID0369150 was raised.
If the module has indeed been replaced, please provide us with the service report.
Additionally, according to the service technician, the charger is classified as an ERK. To carry out repairs on the measurement parts, state-certified permission is required. This leads us to believe that the customer might have tried to avoid replacing the cable.
When we checked on 28.08.2024, by disconnecting the J4 connector from state monitor KF14, we observed errors related to the temperature and contact sensor in the outlet, which were reported on the SCB. Based on this, we reviewed the logs on AWS and found that this error was recorded over 400 times.
Please refer to the attached snapshot, which shows the error count.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav Malokar

additional_info.body:
Dear Mr. Sascha,
I hope you are doing well.
Upon reviewing the logs for this charger since its commissioning, we noticed that there has not been a single successful charging session on outlet 1. If the charger was successfully commissioned at the beginning, could you please provide us with the commissioning report and details of who conducted this activity? Additionally, could you confirm if successful charging sessions were performed on both outlets during commissioning?
As we did the intervention with service technician on 28.08.2024, when we disconnected the J4 connector from state monitor KF14, we observed errors related to the temperature and contact sensor in outlet 1, which were also reported on the SCB. Upon reviewing the AWS logs, we found that this error was recorded over 400 times. Since there is no possibility or provision for cable sensor replacement, we would need to replace the entire cable.
To conclude the root cause of the issue, we cannot make a determination remotely without replacing the cable. It could be an issue with the state monitor KF14 or possibly the KF12 module, which is being used for outlet 1. Additionally, we observed some sessions where contactor QA21-22 showed abnormalities, which should also be considered during the upcoming intervention plan.
And we cannot comment on the cost responsibility, as that decision lies outside our NOC's scope.
Please let me know if you have any further insights or require additional information. If the requested information is satisfactory, could we proceed to move this ticket to your queue for further course of action?
Thank you.
